metadata.title: How to make Jambalaya Creole Style
metadata.description:
This delicious one pot hearty dish is bursting full of Creole flavour.  I hope you enjoy making this easy Jambalaya.

I’m Caroline Artiss, I trained as a chef, been in the food world for 20 years and I'm a single mom so I am an expert in making quick, easy, tasty and mostly healthy recipes for very busy people.  
I’m also a cook book author, recipe and food product developer, I helped open and consulted on my restaurant  “The Gorgeous Kitchen” at London Heathrow Terminal 2, with 3 other British female chefs. 
If you’re ever flying through make sure you stop in!! ☺
I started filming and editing all my own recipes on YouTube 6 years ago as I love teaching people how to cook and it’s lead to some amazing things happening in my life.  My biggest wish is that you find my recipes easy, affordable, and yummy!  Enjoy and leave your comments! Nom nom nom...

nodes.plm_caption:
A woman showing how to cook a dish in a cast iron pot. She cooks shrimp, rice, and vegetables. The video ends with a closeup of the dish in a plate.
The woman is wearing a jean shirt and she has long black hair. She is standing in front of the pan while stirring the ingredients. In the background, there is a sink, cupboards, a window and some flower pots.
A black cast iron pot is on a stove with no flame. The ingredients being cooked are chicken, rice, some green and red vegetables, sausage, curry, pepper and chili powder. The pan is covered with foil while cooking. Shrimp is added at the end of the clip.

summary.brief: The presenter cooks Creole jambalaya in a cast‑iron pot, adds shrimp, garnishes it, and then tastes the finished dish.
summary.detailed: The video opens with the presenter standing at a kitchen counter beside a cutting board of chopped vegetables. She heats a few tablespoons of canola oil in a black cast‑iron pot, browns chicken thigh pieces and sliced sausage, then adds minced garlic, onion, celery and green bell pepper. She seasons the mixture with Creole seasoning, thyme, oregano and a diced jalapeño, and drops in a couple of bay leaves. After the aromatics soften, she stirs in uncooked rice so it coats the flavors, adds chopped tomatoes and chicken stock, covers the pot with foil and lets it simmer gently. Near the end she folds in several shrimp, lets them cook briefly, uncovers, fluffs the jambalaya, sprinkles sliced spring onions on top, and plates the dish. The presenter then sits at a kitchen island, tastes the jambalaya with a spoon, smiles and comments on its flavor before the video ends.

action.detailed: Heat oil in the cast‑iron pot, brown the chicken and sausage, add garlic, onion, celery and green pepper, season with Creole seasoning, thyme, oregano and jalapeño, stir in the rice, pour in tomatoes and chicken stock, cover with foil and simmer, fold in the shrimp, then fluff, garnish with spring onions and serve.
action.actor: the woman in a denim shirt with long black hair who demonstrates the recipe

The camera pans to a bowl of the finished jambalaya, finished with a sprinkle of spring onions.

summary.brief: The chef cooks Creole jambalaya in a cast‑iron skillet, browning chicken (and sausage), adding vegetables, rice and seasonings, then finishing with shrimp and a spring‑onion garnish.
summary.detailed: The presenter heats a few tablespoons of canola oil in a large black cast‑iron skillet on a gas stove, browns bite‑size pieces of chicken (and sausage) until lightly colored, then adds minced garlic, diced onion, chopped celery and green bell pepper. She seasons the mixture with a tablespoon of Creole seasoning, a pinch of thyme, oregano and bay leaves, and an extra jalapeño for heat, letting everything simmer together. After the chicken is nearly cooked she stirs in uncooked rice to coat it with the flavorful juices, follows with chopped tomatoes and chicken stock, and covers the skillet with foil and a lid to let the rice steam until tender. Near the end she adds a dash of Worcestershire sauce (and optional hot sauce), drops raw shrimp into the pan, reseals it briefly until the shrimp turn pink, then uncovers, fluffs the jambalaya, sprinkles chopped spring onions on top and serves the dish on a white plate with a red‑floral rim.

action.detailed: Heat oil in a cast‑iron skillet, brown the chicken and sausage, add garlic, onion, celery and green pepper, season with Creole spice, thyme, oregano, bay leaves and jalapeño, stir in the rice to coat, pour in chopped tomatoes and chicken stock, cover with foil and simmer until the rice is tender, then stir in the shrimp, cook briefly until pink, garnish with spring onions and serve.

summary_sent_to_llm.title: How to make Jambalaya Creole Style
summary_sent_to_llm.description:
This delicious one pot hearty dish is bursting full of Creole flavour.  I hope you enjoy making this easy Jambalaya.

I’m Caroline Artiss, I trained as a chef, been in the food world for 20 years and I'm a single mom so I am an expert in making quick, easy, tasty and mostly healthy recipes for very busy people.  
I’m also a cook book author, recipe and food product developer, I helped open and consulted on my restaurant  “The Gorgeous Kitchen” at London Heathrow Terminal 2, with 3 other British female chefs. 
If you’re ever flying through make sure you stop in!! ☺
I started filming and editing
summary_sent_to_llm.root_summary: The video opens with the presenter standing at a kitchen counter beside a cutting board of chopped vegetables. She heats a few tablespoons of canola oil in a black cast‑iron pot, browns chicken thigh pieces and sliced sausage, then adds minced garlic, onion, celery and green bell pepper. She seasons the mixture with Creole seasoning, thyme, oregano and a diced jalapeño, and drops in a couple of bay leaves. After the aromatics soften, she stirs in uncooked rice so it coats the flavors, adds chopped tomatoes and chicken stock, covers the pot with foil and lets it simmer gently. Near the end she folds in several shrimp, lets them cook briefly, uncovers, fluffs the jambalaya, sprinkles sliced spring onions on top, and plates the dish. The presenter then sits at a kitchen island, tastes the jambalaya with a spoon, smiles and comments on its flavor before the video ends.
